idiom_name: async let / withTaskGroup collecting child-task results
implementation_notes: Swift concurrency is part of the language: async let binds a fixed set of child tasks and awaiting the bindings performs the wait-for-all aggregation, while withTaskGroup (withThrowingTaskGroup) fans out a dynamic number of partials and collects them with for await result in group; structured concurrency guarantees that when the collecting scope exits no partial is still running. Time-out and first-best conditions are not provided: race the group against Task.sleep, use a deadline helper, or Combine's Publishers.Zip/Merge when the partials are already publishers.
pitfalls: A throwing task group fails fast: the first thrown error cancels the remaining children and the aggregate is never built - use withTaskGroup with Result values when partial results must be published.
Cancellation in Swift is cooperative: ask() must check Task.isCancelled (or use APIs that do), or cancelled group children still run to completion.
Accumulating into an array is safe only because the parent consumes the group serially; sharing mutable state across children requires an actor or a lock.
